chunks: Saad ibn Abdullah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Hammad ibn Uthman who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who uproots a tree from his grazing area or his house within the Haram (sanctuary). He said: 'If the tree had remained there before he built the house or established the grazing area, he is not allowed to uproot it. And if it was new (planted by him) upon it, then he has the right to uproot it.'

key_terms.طَرِيَّةً: new or fresh (referring to recent planting)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on uprooting trees in the Haram if they were there before or after building a house?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the principle of ownership continuity within the Haram sanctuary, distinguishing between pre-existing natural vegetation and owner-planted trees. It establishes that one cannot uproot trees that predate their property acquisition, preserving the sanctity and original state of the holy land, while allowing removal of subsequently planted ones. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on balancing private property rights with the preservation of the Haram’s intrinsic sanctity.
